dedupe_keys.name: kempten industrial waste heat district heating gis workflow

description: Hochschule Kempten publishes a notebook workflow for locating German industrial waste-heat sources relative to district-heating demand areas. The sequence cleans the BfEE Plattform für Abwärme 2025 table, geocodes facilities, classifies heat-source descriptions, computes road-network distances with OSMnx and NetworkX, joins to heating-area polygons and creates maps. The README identifies the external district-heating-area input from sEEnergies and warns that BfEE source data have separate usage conditions; the project’s MIT licence applies to its code. Nominatim geocoding is rate limited. The authors say this is a reproducible analysis workflow, not a general production library. This review opened the README, provider landing page and repository tree, but did not run notebooks, download input tables or check geocoding accuracy. Its direct example is Germany, while adapted code may be useful elsewhere with new source inputs. A modeller could use the prepared proximity features to screen waste-heat supply for a district-heating capacity scenario. Related catalogue resources data-bfee-germany-waste-heat-platform and data-europe-district-heating-areas-excess-heat-potentials supply source data, not this joining workflow.
licence: MIT for project code; BfEE PfA and sEEnergies input-data rights remain separate.
